blocking.issue: New regression from the L4X-5 fix: S5x cannot meet PB-14. S5x adds 1 ms of delay in each direction, so every GCRA call has a floor of 2 ms of injected delay. The call also pays the base RH-1 round trip, 50 µs or less (hypothesis), plus Valkey script time. Every sample is therefore above 2 ms, so PB-14's 2 ms p99 fails on every run. blocking.section: Benchmark methodology (Scenarios, O1 and the S2 Bundle); Benchmark suite and CI gating (Constants the suite verifies)
blocking.issue: New issue in the L4X-1 fix: the Upstream semaphore stops O1 long before the in-flight ceiling. The bench Upstream `mock` sets no `circuitBreaker`, so the defaults from Traffic management and resilience apply: `maxConnections` 1,024, `maxPendingRequests` 256, and a single Endpoint limited to 50% of `maxConnections`, which is 512 attempts. In O1a the mock delays each response by 1 s, and 20,000 rps are to be admitted. That needs about 20,000 concurrent Upstream attempts, but only about 512 can hold the semaphore and 256 can wait. Everything else gets 503 `RZ-UP-006` at once. In-flight units therefore never approach 20,000 and `RZ-RT-005` is never emitted, so O1a fails every one of its own pass criteria. In O1b about 20,000 admitted requests queue for about 0.54 s (hypothesis). Many of them hold or wait for the semaphore, so `RZ-UP-006` also contaminates 'excess only as `RZ-RT-005`'. The Bundle also breaks the Traffic management rule that '`maxConnections` SHOULD exceed attempts per second per Node' in S1 and S2, which run at 40,000 to 50,000 attempts per second. Failure scenario: the 20,000-unit shedding path again goes unexercised, and a benchmark run hides the production misconfiguration it should expose.
blocking.evidence: L308 'O1a: mock delay 1 s, 30,000 rps, 150% of what the in-flight ceiling admits ... active requests plateau at 20,000'; L353-361 the `mock` Upstream has one Endpoint and no `circuitBreaker`; Traffic management: '`circuitBreaker` limits | `maxConnections` 1,024, `maxPendingRequests` 256' and '`maxPendingRequests` | ... | 503 `RZ-UP-006` at once' and 'An Endpoint holds at most max(8, min(2 × its weighted share, 50%) of `maxConnections`) in-flight attempts'.
blocking.fix: Give the bench Upstream `circuitBreaker: {maxConnections: 65536, maxPendingRequests: 1024}` (target). Both fields are defined in the Configuration model. Put it in the base Bundle so that S1 and S2 also meet the attempts-per-second rule. Alternatively, add it only to an O1 overlay with at least two mock Endpoints, so that the per-Endpoint 50% share covers 20,000 attempts. Add 'zero `RZ-UP-006`' to O1's pass criteria. Also record the ephemeral port range needed for about 20,000 HTTP/1.1 connections to the mock among the recorded sysctls.

blocking.section: Startup and reload time by configuration size (Fleet-level timing); Benchmark methodology (Scenarios, F2)
blocking.issue: Partly resolved: F2 exists now, but as specified it cannot verify the per-replica stream capacity it is assigned. F2 runs 10,000 emulated Nodes against three replicas, so each replica holds about 3,333 streams, never 5,000 and never the onset of shedding. The 5,000-stream figure is what Scalability's HA rule rests on: ceil(N / 5,000) + 1 replicas, so that losing one replica never exceeds stream capacity. At 10,000 Nodes that rule predicts two survivors at exactly 5,000 streams each. F2 has no step that removes a replica, so the one load the rule depends on is never produced. Failure scenario: a replica dies in a 10,000-Node Cluster, and the two survivors take 5,000 streams each for the first time in production. If real capacity is, say, 4,000, both shed, and every shed Node redials, which is the reconnect storm CE-10 is meant to bound.
blocking.evidence: L283 'Control Streams per replica before shedding | 5,000 (hypothesis) | F2'; L315 'F2 | A Control Stream driver emulating 10,000 Nodes ... against three replicas'; Scalability: 'deployments SHOULD run at least ceil(N / 5,000) + 1 replicas across zones (hypothesis), so losing one never exceeds stream capacity'; Cell and Cluster bottlenecks: 'Ruralz Control streams | About 5,000 per replica (hypothesis) | `Reconnect` with `shed`'.
blocking.fix: Add two F2 steps. First, stop one of the three replicas, so that 10,000 streams settle on two, and pass when neither survivor sheds and every Node reconnects within 5 minutes (target). Second, drive a single replica past 5,000 streams to find where shedding starts, and record that point as the measured capacity that replaces the hypothesis. Use `ruralz_control_connected_nodes` and `Reconnect` with `reason: shed` as the signals.
